dataset.kind: live public Web, HTTP(S) GET, no authentication
dataset.site_sample_source: prereg.md section 5.2, fixed before any request
dataset.concurrency: 5 worker threads, one strictly sequential request queue per host, so the per-host rate limit holds by construction
dataset.fetch_window_utc: 2026-09-27T02:32:12Z to 2026-09-27T02:32:49Z (37 s of page GETs; robots.txt fetches span 2026-09-27T02:32:12Z to 2026-09-27T02:32:43Z). 5 concurrent workers, one sequential queue per host.
dataset.robots_txt: fetched once per host before any page request and honoured. 18 of 20 hosts returned a parsable robots.txt: 16 returned HTTP 200. stackoverflow.com returned HTTP 418 and www.npmjs.com returned HTTP 403, neither of which is a robots.txt body, so no rules were parsed and none were applied for those two hosts. git-scm.com and kernel.org returned 404 and were treated as unrestricted per prereg 13. Three hosts had same-origin URLs disallowed by robots and were not crawled past them: en.wikipedia.org (4, all /wiki/Special:*), gnu.org (1), news.ycombinator.com (1).

None is recorded as a negative result and none was retried with a different User-Agent, renderer or sample, because prereg 5.2 fixes the sample and prereg 5.3/6.1 fix discovery and headers.
dataset.not_measured_corroboration: The robots.txt fetches independently corroborate the two HTTP-403 homepage blocks: www.npmjs.com/robots.txt returned 403 and stackoverflow.com/robots.txt returned 418. The block is therefore host-level edge behaviour under the frozen User-Agent, not a per-path decision by these sites.
